transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I keep getting stuck on this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek. I notice it a lot in photos and under the store lights. Other people say they don’t see it, but it feels like it’s the first thing customers or my managers notice when they look at me.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or examining that spot on your face?

Yeah. On my breaks I usually go to the bathroom and look at it in the mirror, and I’ll try to fix my hair so it covers that area. I also compare myself to girls who come through my line. Sometimes I lose track of time doing it and end up late getting back to the register.
When you feel upset in these situations, is it mainly because you believe that spot on your face looks noticeably wrong or ugly to other people?

Yeah. It feels like that uneven spot is really obvious, especially in photos or under the store lights. Even though people tell me they don’t notice it, I keep thinking customers or my managers see it first.
Do you avoid social situations because you’re afraid people will notice that spot on your face?
I’m not really sure. I still go to work and things, but I do worry about people looking at it.
Have you ever skipped work, canceled plans, or left a situation because you felt too self-conscious about that spot on your face?

I haven’t skipped work, but it’s been affecting me there. My manager’s noticed I’m late coming back from breaks and slower at the register, and I’m worried I look unreliable, especially since I’m trying to get promoted.
Do you believe there is actually something wrong with how that area of your face looks?

Yeah, I do. It’s a tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek, but in photos or under the store lights it looks really noticeable to me. Other people say they can’t see it, but I feel like it’s the first thing customers or my managers notice.
If that spot on your face looked exactly the way you wanted, would you still feel very anxious about people looking at you?
I think I’d feel a lot less anxious. It’s really that spot—I keep noticing it in pictures and under the store lights, and then I feel like everyone else must be noticing it too.
Do you ever think that maybe other people really cannot see that spot the way you do?

Sometimes I wonder if they really don’t see it, especially when they tell me they don’t. But then I see it in a photo or under the store lights, and it feels so obvious that I have a hard time believing they wouldn’t notice.
Aside from worries about that spot on your face, do you get other unwanted thoughts that keep bothering you over and over?
Not really. Mostly it’s just the spot on my face that I keep thinking about.
